findings: The candidate preserves the recovered source request: mirror a binary tree and provide both recursive and non-recursive implementations.
In-place mutation, int node values, null handling and the ordinary acyclic-tree model are explicitly labelled as candidate API choices rather than recovered source facts.
The recursive implementation follows the structural definition of a mirror by mapping the original right subtree to the new left subtree and vice versa.
The iterative implementation visits every reachable node exactly once with an explicit DFS stack and swaps left/right references once per node.
The O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary-space claims match both implementations; the candidate explicitly calls out recursive stack-overflow risk on a highly skewed tree.

The fixture checks a known asymmetric tree, same-root in-place semantics, double-mirror involution, 4000 deterministic randomized trees against an independent structural oracle, and a 20000-edge skewed tree with the iterative implementation.
The answer does not fabricate a named online-judge problem, production incident or hidden constraint.
Human approval remains a separate pilot promotion gate.
